summary: Hourly meter namespace collision causing split invoice lines across subaccounts
description:
Issue summary: Customer BrightReply reports that a subset of their hourly usage is appearing as separate invoice line items under two different subaccount IDs after a scheduled multi-queue batch run. The split appears to map identical usage timestamps to two 'meter namespaces'.

Impact: BrightReply sees duplicated-looking (split) charges on last billing run that together equal expected usage but are attributed to different subaccounts. This breaks their internal chargeback and forecasting; they request a provisional credit and a root-cause explanation.

Environment: prod, multi-tenant org with subaccounts; observed in us-west and eu-central billing runs for date range 2026-03-07 00:00 - 2026-03-07 08:00 UTC.

Steps to reproduce (as provided by customer):
1) Start a multi-queue batch embedding job that fans out to two worker pools (pool-a and pool-b) using the same API key with subaccount header set.
2) Job retries on queue handoff for a small fraction (~2%) of microbatches.
3) After job completion, BrightReply runs reconciliation and sees some hourly usage posted to subaccount A and some to subaccount B with the same origin request IDs and identical token counts.

Expected behavior: All usage for a given request ID and subaccount header should be attributed to one subaccount and one meter namespace.

Actual behavior: The usage is split between two meter namespaces, creating two invoice lines that sum to the expected usage but are split across subaccounts, causing incorrect chargeback.

Logs/attachments: Customer provided CSV of sample request IDs and corresponding invoice lines, timestamped postback logs, and request-level trace IDs (attached to ticket). They also shared a short Slack thread linking #billing and #support.
comments: 2026-03-10 Support - Sofia Patel: Acknowledged. First response sent to customer, asked for CSV of sample request IDs and the raw postback payloads. Requested the billing window and any retries they observed. Promised update within 24 hours.

2026-03-10 Customer - BrightReply (account lead: Aaron Delgado): Uploaded CSV of 34 sample request IDs. Notes: the requests were originated from a single submit endpoint; internal logs show a transparent retry between worker pools. They attached the retry trace and IDs.
2026-03-11 Support - Sofia Patel: Triage complete. Escalated to Metering team. Added labels and opened linked internal ticket INT-3398 for scheduler handoff investigation.

2026-03-12 Engineering - Daniel Kim: Initial investigation: found that when a microbatch is handed off between queues, our postback reconciler can reuse an internal meter namespace token if the subaccount header is present in one handoff but lost in the retry path. Reproducer in staging created. Marking potential root cause as 'namespace token reuse on cross-queue retry'.

2026-03-13 Engineering - Daniel Kim: Confirmed repro: in multi-queue handoff scenarios, the 'meter_namespace' field in the outgoing postback can be computed from the in-flight worker context; if the handoff loses the explicit subaccount header, reconciler falls back to a computed default namespace (derived from org ID vs subaccount ID), causing split attribution. Patch proposed in PR 4521.

2026-03-14 Support - Sofia Patel: Informed customer: provisional credit offered for affected invoice lines while engineering prepares fix. Requested permission to apply temporary centralized billing mapping to combine the two namespaces for BrightReply's billing cycle. Customer accepted provisional credit and mapping.
investigation_notes: Collected 34 sample request IDs and traced postback sequences across the scheduler and reconciler component logs.
Observed two distinct meter_namespace values in postbacks for identical request IDs: one namespaced by subaccount header, the other defaulting to org-level namespace.
Reproduction steps confirmed in staging: forcing a queue handoff without propagating X-Subaccount header leads to computed fallback namespace during postback emission.

Hypothesis: race condition in handoff code path where context propagation middleware does not guarantee subaccount header preservation when retrying between worker pools. The reconciler aggregates hourly buckets based on meter_namespace, causing split invoice lines.
Impact estimate: approximately 1.8% of BrightReply's hourly usage during the window; some customers with high fanout/multi-queue jobs may see similar symptoms at low frequency.

Related code area: scheduler/handshake middleware, postback emission path, meter namespace derivation logic. See PR 4521 for proposed fix to always preserve explicit subaccount header in handoff metadata.
Linked internal issue INT-3398 tracks adding end-to-end unit tests to prevent regression.
Data retention note: collected reconciler logs and CSV samples stored in secured S3 bucket s3://redwood-support-artifacts/SUP-820419/ (access limited to billing and engineering).
resolution_notes: Temporary workaround applied (2026-03-14 by Billing Ops): centralized billing mapping rule added to treat the two detected meter_namespace values as a single namespace for BrightReply for the affected billing window. This produces combined invoice lines in the provisional invoice export.

Provisional credit: Finance approved a provisional credit equal to the smaller of the two invoice lines for the affected window. Customer accepted credit and requested final reconciliation after permanent fix.

Permanent fix: merged PR https://github.com/redwood/usage-reconciler/pull/4521 contains code to ensure subaccount header is preserved across queue handoffs and adds a reconciliation check that rejects ambiguous namespace postbacks. Targeted rollout to prod on 2026-03-20 with canary in us-west first.
Post-deploy action items: run a replay job over 2026-03-07 to validate no further split attribution; update billing run reconciliation to flag namespace collisions; backfill credits where necessary.
Customer communication: Support to send final reconciliation note and updated invoice on 2026-03-21. Recommend closing ticket when customer confirms final invoice matches expectations.

Follow-up: Engineering to add integration test to CI for multi-queue handoff scenarios and update runbook for billing ops to detect meter namespace collisions automatically. INT-3398 will track tests and runbook update.
Status: In Progress. Patch merged to main, deploy scheduled; provisional credit applied. Awaiting post-deploy verification and customer sign-off.
